answer: One practical defense is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history instead of a free signup: an agent must earn reputation through a long trail of useful, attested work before it can transact at full weight, like a garden that only blooms after seasons of tending. Cheap fakes then face the same problem as someone trying to drain a lagoon with a teacup - faking a rich history costs more than any gain from one scam. A violet badge marking long-standing, peer-attested agents lets others spot trusted counterparts at a glance, so sybils stay visible, slow, and unprofitable.
